You are resuming a Ralph Workflow PLANNING EDIT MODE session that has already failed THREE times due to inactivity timeouts. Do NOT restart from scratch — work efficiently and avoid any long-running or stalling operations. Complete the task in this single run.

## Context to read first (in order)
1. `/REDACTED_WORKSPACE/.agent/tmp/planning_master_prompt.md` — binding master instructions for this session.
2. `/REDACTED_WORKSPACE/.agent/PRODUCT_CRITERIA.md` — authoritative task/product criteria (source of truth for the goal).
3. `/REDACTED_WORKSPACE/.agent/PLANNING_ANALYSIS_DECISION.md` — analysis feedback from a fresh reviewer on the existing plan.
4. `/REDACTED_WORKSPACE/.agent/tmp/planning_prompt.md` — the original prompt for this task.
5. Retry context files (read whichever exist, most recent last), for what's already been attempted/learned:
   - `/REDACTED_WORKSPACE/.agent/tmp/agent_retry_context_3f1c9c7cf92f45a0984631038b97c5fa.md`
   - `/REDACTED_WORKSPACE/.agent/tmp/agent_retry_context_a581a83e79ef41e5a8c4dc229c6b53d2.md`
   - `/REDACTED_WORKSPACE/.agent/tmp/agent_retry_context_a556c82257f245b9bbc2244080ca156c.md`
6. Check for an existing plan draft via `mcp__ralph__ralph_get_md_draft` (artifact_type="plan") to see what's already staged, and also check `mcp__ralph__ralph_index_status` / `mcp__ralph__git_status` if useful.

## Task
This is PLANNING EDIT MODE: revise the current plan artifact using fresh repository evidence and the analysis feedback in PLANNING_ANALYSIS_DECISION.md. You are working in a Ralph Workflow brokered session — you have MCP tools prefixed `mcp__ralph__` available (read_file, list_directory, grep_files, search_files, git_status, git_diff, git_log, exec, ralph_get_md_draft, ralph_edit_md_artifact, ralph_stage_md_artifact, ralph_submit_md_artifact, ralph_verify_md_artifact, ralph_finalize_md_artifact, ralph_discard_md_draft, declare_complete, etc.). Use ONLY these brokered tools for workspace reads/writes — do not use native Bash/Read/Write/Edit for the workspace (this session has policy flag `no_edit` and capabilities are brokered-only). You may use WebSearch/WebFetch equivalents only if genuinely needed; prefer the ralph web tools if available.

Steps:
1. Gather evidence: read the current plan draft (if any exists from prior failed attempts), the product criteria, and the analysis feedback. Use `mcp__ralph__grep_files`/`mcp__ralph__read_file`/`mcp__ralph__git_log`/`mcp__ralph__git_diff` etc. to verify any file/behavior claims in the plan against the actual repository — do not guess.
2. Identify what analysis feedback requires changing in the plan. Keep valid existing material; update every affected commitment together per the analysis feedback (it's substantive advice, not a formatting checklist).
3. Produce/revise the plan per the format guide at `.agent/artifact-formats/plan.md` (read it via mcp__ralph__read_file). Use `### [S-n] Title` steps with stable IDs; use `Type: verify` for verification steps. Record any deliberate override of a warning/info diagnostic under `## Validation Overrides` with reasoning.
4. Submit the plan:
   - If there's an existing draft that's close, use `mcp__ralph__ralph_edit_md_artifact` with targeted oldText/newText edits (dry_run first if unsure).
   - If a wholesale rewrite is genuinely needed, use `mcp__ralph__ralph_stage_md_artifact` with `mode="replace_all"`, then `mcp__ralph__ralph_finalize_md_artifact`.
   - Otherwise use `mcp__ralph__ralph_submit_md_artifact` directly with the full document.
   - Check the response for diagnostics; PLAN001 is the only blocking one. Fix and resubmit until it validates (or diagnostics are only warnings/info, which you may override with recorded reasoning).
5. Once you get a valid submission receipt, call `mcp__ralph__declare_complete` as your FINAL action. This is mandatory to end the phase.

## Constraints to avoid another timeout
- Do not wait idly. Do not perform excessive redundant re-reading. Work directly toward submitting a valid plan and declaring complete.
- Do not spawn further sub-agents or ask for confirmation — this is unattended/autonomous mode with no interactive response path.
- Do not write any status `.md` files outside of the `.agent` artifact submission flow.
- Report back a concise final summary of what you did and confirmation that `declare_complete` was called successfully.

# Contractor surface — change batch 1

Work the contractor course-plan builder through the spec below. Read `AGENTS.md`
and the policies in `docs/ralph-workflow-policy/` before changing anything, and
use `make verify` as the authoritative gate before claiming any item done.

Each item gives the request **verbatim**, the **decision** taken on it, and
**acceptance criteria**. Where the original request was ambiguous, the decision
records the call and the reasoning. Do not widen scope past these criteria; if
an item turns out to be wrong, say so rather than silently redesigning it.

Two screenshots accompany this batch:

- **Screenshot A** — the course plan builder today: the
  `within 2 weeks students will be able to…` watermark, the course/round context
  line, the milestone and activity boxes, and the current placement of the move
  up / move down / delete controls. Most layout items below describe this screen.
- **Screenshot B** — milestone vs activity type hierarchy, for the font item.

## What already exists (do not rebuild)

Verified in the codebase before writing this spec:

- **Activity minutes already exist.** `course_plan_activities.time_value_min`
  (integer, default 0, not null). `_course_milestone.html.erb` already renders
  `"… min in this milestone"`, and `CoursePlan#recompute_totals!` already
  maintains `course_plan.totals_min` (excluding `synthesis` activities).
- **AI assist already exists.** `app/views/shared/plan_builder/_ai_assist.html.erb`
  — a modal with a plan prompt, Generate, and replace / amend / append apply
  modes, driven by the `plan-ai-assist` Stimulus controller.
- **Move up / Move down / Delete already exist** in `_course_milestone.html.erb`.
- **Plan editability is already governed by status**, not schedule:
  `CoursePlan#editable?` is `draft? || needs_revision?`, enforced in
  `CoursePlanMilestonesController#load_course_plan`.
- **The LLM stack is provider-generic.** `Llm::Client` is the single chat
  transport seam and resolves the active provider at call time from
  `SiteAiSetting` / `OrganizationAiSetting`, so a SUP can switch providers
  without code changes. `SiteAiSetting::SUPPORTED_PROVIDERS` is
  `%w[openai gemini]`, `AiCredential` already holds credentials for both
  (`openai_api_key` / `openai_api_base` and the Vertex AI service-account
  fields), and `LlmModelCatalogEntry` carries a `provider` column. **No item in
  this batch should name or add a specific provider** — anything AI-facing goes
  through the existing seam and works with whichever provider is configured.

## Checklist

### 1. Milestone add / reorder is broken

> **Adding Milestones and moving them up or down in the plan is broken. Please
> make operations …**

The request is cut off mid-sentence. Rather than guess the missing clause, the
behaviour was diagnosed directly. **Three independent root causes**, all real:

1. **Mixed position bases.** `next_position`
   (`CoursePlanMilestonesController:131`) returns `maximum(:position).to_i + 1`,
   so the *first* milestone in a plan gets position **1**. But
   `reorder_milestones!` (:142) and `restore` (:61) renormalise to a **0**-based
   dense index. A never-reordered plan is 1-based; one reorder silently converts
   it to 0-based. The "Move up" disabled check in the view is
   `milestone.position.zero?`, which never fires on a 1-based plan — so the
   first milestone shows an **enabled "Move up" button that does nothing**.
2. **`destroy` never renormalises.** It only sets `discarded_at`
   (:42–50), so positions develop gaps — `[0, 2, 3]`. The view computes
   `position - 1` / `position + 1` from the *stored* position, but
   `reorder_milestones!` treats the incoming number as an *index* into the
   ordered sibling list (`siblings.insert(target, …)`). Once positions have
   gaps, stored position ≠ index, so "Move up" from stored position 2 resolves
   to index 1 — where the milestone already sits. **No-op, or a two-slot jump.**
   `CoursePlanActivitiesController#destroy` has the identical defect.
3. **Turbo-frame lock staleness.** `respond_to_milestone_mutation` (:169)
   re-renders only the mutated milestone's frame, but
   `lock_course_plan_for_mutation` (:103) bumps the parent plan's `lock_version`
   on every successful mutation. Every *other* milestone frame still embeds the
   old `lock_version`, and `verify_course_plan_lock` (:87) rejects any mismatch
   — so the next click on a different milestone 409s with
   **"This plan changed in another session. Reload it and try again."**

**Decision:** make `position` a dense, 0-based index that is authoritative after
every mutation, and stop doing arithmetic on stored positions in the view.

Acceptance criteria:

- [ ] `next_position` and the renormalise paths agree on a single 0-based
      convention. A plan's positions are always `0..n-1` with no gaps.
- [ ] `destroy` renormalises surviving siblings — milestones **and** activities.
- [ ] Move up / down send the target **index derived from the rendered order**,
      not `stored_position ± 1`.
- [ ] "Move up" is disabled on the first milestone and "Move down" on the last,
      including immediately after a delete.
- [ ] Two consecutive mutations on *different* milestones both succeed with no
      reload — no spurious stale-plan 409.
- [ ] Regression tests cover: reorder after delete, reorder on a fresh plan, and
      back-to-back mutations on different milestones.

### 2. Preround contractor

> **Preround Contractor. Are we in the round or before the round**

**Decision: informational and navigational only — not a second permission gate.**
Plan editability is already governed by plan status. Layering a schedule-based
lock on top creates states where a plan is `draft` (so the UI offers editing)
but blocked for schedule reasons, with no recovery path for the contractor.
Show *where we are*; let status keep deciding *what's allowed*.

Acceptance criteria:

- [ ] Contractor surfaces show whether the round is before start or in progress.
- [ ] The state comes from `Round#student_start_state`
      (`:unknown` / `:future` / `:past`) — do not add a second predicate, and do
      not read `created_at` as schedule data.
- [ ] `:unknown` (no published schedule) renders no preround claim at all.
- [ ] No editing permission changes in this item.

### 3. Watermarks

> **Watermark within 2 weeks students will be able to…** (Screenshot A)
>
> **Also remove the "optional….purpose" watermark.**

The second is `app/views/contractor_course_plans/new.html.erb:34` —
`Optional. State what students will learn or make so the first milestone has a
clear purpose.`

Acceptance criteria:

- [ ] Both watermarks removed from the course plan surface.
- [ ] Removing helper copy does not orphan an `aria-describedby` reference.

### 4. Ten capture boxes

> **Add an extension on the course plan page or 10 boxes that allow contractors
> to type in, upload or speak/LLM Generate**

**Decision: ten numbered source-material slots on the course plan page, each
accepting typed text, a file upload, or dictation, feeding the existing AI
assist as source material.** Reading "extension … or 10 boxes" as two names for
one feature, and "type in, upload or speak" as three input modes for a single
box rather than three separate features. They feed the existing
`plan_draft` apply pipeline instead of a parallel generator.

Acceptance criteria:

- [ ] Ten slots on the course plan page, each supporting all three input modes.
- [ ] Slots may be left blank; empty slots contribute nothing.
- [ ] Contents feed the existing assist and land through the existing
      replace / amend / append modes.
- [ ] Uploads honour the accept-type and size limits already used by the guide
      import; dictation degrades gracefully where unsupported.
- [ ] Generation goes through the existing `Llm::Client` seam and behaves the
      same under whichever provider the site is configured for. No
      provider-specific branch, no new transport, no new credential fields.
- [ ] An unconfigured or disabled AI provider degrades to a clear message — the
      slots still accept typed text, uploads and dictation.

### 5. Plan builder layout

> **Would prefer the Milestone font bolded and larger than the activity font**
> (Screenshot B)
>
> **`## Biology AM / 2026 Early August — Round 1 — Spring Field Study / AM`
> Make that the light grey**
>
> **Second box is the milestone which expands to the the activities**
>
> **Move move up, move down and delete over to the right.**
>
> **Add Acitivity button that expands and collapses activities**
>
> **Default 1 Milestones and 2 activities that are left blank**

All on `_course_milestone.html.erb` / `_course_activity.html.erb` and the
course-plan show page.

Acceptance criteria:

- [ ] Milestone heading is visibly bolder and larger than activity text.
- [ ] The course / round context line renders light grey.
- [ ] The milestone is the second box and expands to reveal its activities.
- [ ] Move up / Move down / Delete sit right-aligned in their row.
- [ ] "Add Activity" both adds an activity and expands/collapses the list. The
      add form is currently always expanded — it should collapse by default.
- [ ] A new course plan seeds one empty milestone with two empty activities.
- [ ] Seeded blanks do not trip required-field validation before the contractor
      has typed anything, and do not count toward the minutes total.
- [ ] Type styles come from the design system —
      `docs/ralph-workflow-policy/design-system-policy.md`, gate
      `script/design_system_guard.sh`. No ad-hoc font sizes or hex greys.
- [ ] Controls keep their 44px minimum touch target.

### 6. Minutes must meet the course requirement

> **Minutes for activities will equate or surpass total number of minutes
> required for course**

Activity minutes and the plan total already exist. **The only missing piece is
the course-level requirement** — `courses` has no such column.

**Decision: add `courses.required_minutes` (integer, nullable). Warn while
drafting; block at submit-for-approval. Null means no requirement and no gate.**
The requirement belongs to the course, not to one contractor's plan — if each
plan set its own target the constraint would be self-certifying. Blocking every
save would make incremental plan building impossible, so enforcement lands at
the submit gate; null keeps existing courses working unchanged.

Acceptance criteria:

- [ ] `courses.required_minutes` added, nullable, admin-editable.
- [ ] The plan shows running total vs requirement and the shortfall.
- [ ] `totals_min >= required_minutes` is enforced on submit-for-approval;
      short plans are blocked with a message naming the shortfall.
- [ ] Draft saves are never blocked by this rule.
- [ ] `required_minutes IS NULL` → no warning, no gate.
- [ ] Comparison uses `CoursePlan#recompute_totals!` / `totals_min` — do not
      introduce a second summation with different `synthesis` handling.

### 7. Student tab date filter

> **Under student tab have a date filter which allows contractor to select a
> date and student in order to approve work done while student was absent or
> other instances.**

Lives under `app/views/staff/students/`.

Acceptance criteria:

- [ ] Filter selects a date **and** a student.
- [ ] From the filtered view the contractor can approve work for that date.
- [ ] Approval is scoped to the contractor's assigned courses — reuse the
      existing `ContractorCourseAssignment` authorisation, do not widen it.
- [ ] Backdated approval is attributable: it records who approved, when, and
      the date approved *for*.

## Open risks

- **Screenshots not machine-readable here.** Items 3 and 5 were written from the
  surrounding text. Confirm the exact watermark field and type targets against
  Screenshot A/B before editing.
- **Item 1's truncated clause** may have named a fourth symptom beyond the three
  diagnosed. The three above are confirmed in code; if a fourth shows up, report
  it rather than folding it in silently.
- **Item 4 is the largest item** — three input modes, ten slots, upload and
  dictation handling. If it needs splitting, split it and say so.

## Constraints

- Follow `docs/ralph-workflow-policy/` — `design-system-policy.md` for view
  work, `testing-policy.md` before tests, `typechecking-policy.md` for typed
  code (this codebase is `# typed: strict` Sorbet), `security-policy.md` for new
  input surfaces, `verification-policy.md` before reporting completion.
- Never touch production key material: `.kamal/app_secrets/`, `.kamal/secrets`,
  `.kamal/app_secrets.fingerprints`, `script/prod_secrets_*`, or the
  `PROD-SECRET-GUARD` regions in `Dockerfile` and `config/application.rb`.

# Contractor surface — change batch 1

Work the contractor course-plan builder through the spec below. Read `AGENTS.md`
and the policies in `docs/ralph-workflow-policy/` before changing anything, and
use `make verify` as the authoritative gate before claiming any item done.

Each item gives the request **verbatim**, the **decision** taken on it, and
**acceptance criteria**. Where the original request was ambiguous, the decision
records the call and the reasoning. Do not widen scope past these criteria; if
an item turns out to be wrong, say so rather than silently redesigning it.

Two screenshots accompany this batch:

- **Screenshot A** — the course plan builder today: the
  `within 2 weeks students will be able to…` watermark, the course/round context
  line, the milestone and activity boxes, and the current placement of the move
  up / move down / delete controls. Most layout items below describe this screen.
- **Screenshot B** — milestone vs activity type hierarchy, for the font item.

## What already exists (do not rebuild)

Verified in the codebase before writing this spec:

- **Activity minutes already exist.** `course_plan_activities.time_value_min`
  (integer, default 0, not null). `_course_milestone.html.erb` already renders
  `"… min in this milestone"`, and `CoursePlan#recompute_totals!` already
  maintains `course_plan.totals_min` (excluding `synthesis` activities).
- **AI assist already exists.** `app/views/shared/plan_builder/_ai_assist.html.erb`
  — a modal with a plan prompt, Generate, and replace / amend / append apply
  modes, driven by the `plan-ai-assist` Stimulus controller.
- **Move up / Move down / Delete already exist** in `_course_milestone.html.erb`.
- **Plan editability is already governed by status**, not schedule:
  `CoursePlan#editable?` is `draft? || needs_revision?`, enforced in
  `CoursePlanMilestonesController#load_course_plan`.
- **The LLM stack is provider-generic.** `Llm::Client` is the single chat
  transport seam and resolves the active provider at call time from
  `SiteAiSetting` / `OrganizationAiSetting`, so a SUP can switch providers
  without code changes. `SiteAiSetting::SUPPORTED_PROVIDERS` is
  `%w[openai gemini]`, `AiCredential` already holds credentials for both
  (`openai_api_key` / `openai_api_base` and the Vertex AI service-account
  fields), and `LlmModelCatalogEntry` carries a `provider` column. **No item in
  this batch should name or add a specific provider** — anything AI-facing goes
  through the existing seam and works with whichever provider is configured.

## Checklist

### 1. Milestone add / reorder is broken

> **Adding Milestones and moving them up or down in the plan is broken. Please
> make operations …**

The request is cut off mid-sentence. Rather than guess the missing clause, the
behaviour was diagnosed directly. **Three independent root causes**, all real:

1. **Mixed position bases.** `next_position`
   (`CoursePlanMilestonesController:131`) returns `maximum(:position).to_i + 1`,
   so the *first* milestone in a plan gets position **1**. But
   `reorder_milestones!` (:142) and `restore` (:61) renormalise to a **0**-based
   dense index. A never-reordered plan is 1-based; one reorder silently converts
   it to 0-based. The "Move up" disabled check in the view is
   `milestone.position.zero?`, which never fires on a 1-based plan — so the
   first milestone shows an **enabled "Move up" button that does nothing**.
2. **`destroy` never renormalises.** It only sets `discarded_at`
   (:42–50), so positions develop gaps — `[0, 2, 3]`. The view computes
   `position - 1` / `position + 1` from the *stored* position, but
   `reorder_milestones!` treats the incoming number as an *index* into the
   ordered sibling list (`siblings.insert(target, …)`). Once positions have
   gaps, stored position ≠ index, so "Move up" from stored position 2 resolves
   to index 1 — where the milestone already sits. **No-op, or a two-slot jump.**
   `CoursePlanActivitiesController#destroy` has the identical defect.
3. **Turbo-frame lock staleness.** `respond_to_milestone_mutation` (:169)
   re-renders only the mutated milestone's frame, but
   `lock_course_plan_for_mutation` (:103) bumps the parent plan's `lock_version`
   on every successful mutation. Every *other* milestone frame still embeds the
   old `lock_version`, and `verify_course_plan_lock` (:87) rejects any mismatch
   — so the next click on a different milestone 409s with
   **"This plan changed in another session. Reload it and try again."**

**Decision:** make `position` a dense, 0-based index that is authoritative after
every mutation, and stop doing arithmetic on stored positions in the view.

Acceptance criteria:

- [ ] `next_position` and the renormalise paths agree on a single 0-based
      convention. A plan's positions are always `0..n-1` with no gaps.
- [ ] `destroy` renormalises surviving siblings — milestones **and** activities.
- [ ] Move up / down send the target **index derived from the rendered order**,
      not `stored_position ± 1`.
- [ ] "Move up" is disabled on the first milestone and "Move down" on the last,
      including immediately after a delete.
- [ ] Two consecutive mutations on *different* milestones both succeed with no
      reload — no spurious stale-plan 409.
- [ ] Regression tests cover: reorder after delete, reorder on a fresh plan, and
      back-to-back mutations on different milestones.

### 2. Preround contractor

> **Preround Contractor. Are we in the round or before the round**

**Decision: informational and navigational only — not a second permission gate.**
Plan editability is already governed by plan status. Layering a schedule-based
lock on top creates states where a plan is `draft` (so the UI offers editing)
but blocked for schedule reasons, with no recovery path for the contractor.
Show *where we are*; let status keep deciding *what's allowed*.

Acceptance criteria:

- [ ] Contractor surfaces show whether the round is before start or in progress.
- [ ] The state comes from `Round#student_start_state`
      (`:unknown` / `:future` / `:past`) — do not add a second predicate, and do
      not read `created_at` as schedule data.
- [ ] `:unknown` (no published schedule) renders no preround claim at all.
- [ ] No editing permission changes in this item.

### 3. Watermarks

> **Watermark within 2 weeks students will be able to…** (Screenshot A)
>
> **Also remove the "optional….purpose" watermark.**

The second is `app/views/contractor_course_plans/new.html.erb:34` —
`Optional. State what students will learn or make so the first milestone has a
clear purpose.`

Acceptance criteria:

- [ ] Both watermarks removed from the course plan surface.
- [ ] Removing helper copy does not orphan an `aria-describedby` reference.

### 4. Ten capture boxes

> **Add an extension on the course plan page or 10 boxes that allow contractors
> to type in, upload or speak/LLM Generate**

**Decision: ten numbered source-material slots on the course plan page, each
accepting typed text, a file upload, or dictation, feeding the existing AI
assist as source material.** Reading "extension … or 10 boxes" as two names for
one feature, and "type in, upload or speak" as three input modes for a single
box rather than three separate features. They feed the existing
`plan_draft` apply pipeline instead of a parallel generator.

Acceptance criteria:

- [ ] Ten slots on the course plan page, each supporting all three input modes.
- [ ] Slots may be left blank; empty slots contribute nothing.
- [ ] Contents feed the existing assist and land through the existing
      replace / amend / append modes.
- [ ] Uploads honour the accept-type and size limits already used by the guide
      import; dictation degrades gracefully where unsupported.
- [ ] Generation goes through the existing `Llm::Client` seam and behaves the
      same under whichever provider the site is configured for. No
      provider-specific branch, no new transport, no new credential fields.
- [ ] An unconfigured or disabled AI provider degrades to a clear message — the
      slots still accept typed text, uploads and dictation.

### 5. Plan builder layout

> **Would prefer the Milestone font bolded and larger than the activity font**
> (Screenshot B)
>
> **`## Biology AM / 2026 Early August — Round 1 — Spring Field Study / AM`
> Make that the light grey**
>
> **Second box is the milestone which expands to the the activities**
>
> **Move move up, move down and delete over to the right.**
>
> **Add Acitivity button that expands and collapses activities**
>
> **Default 1 Milestones and 2 activities that are left blank**

All on `_course_milestone.html.erb` / `_course_activity.html.erb` and the
course-plan show page.

Acceptance criteria:

- [ ] Milestone heading is visibly bolder and larger than activity text.
- [ ] The course / round context line renders light grey.
- [ ] The milestone is the second box and expands to reveal its activities.
- [ ] Move up / Move down / Delete sit right-aligned in their row.
- [ ] "Add Activity" both adds an activity and expands/collapses the list. The
      add form is currently always expanded — it should collapse by default.
- [ ] A new course plan seeds one empty milestone with two empty activities.
- [ ] Seeded blanks do not trip required-field validation before the contractor
      has typed anything, and do not count toward the minutes total.
- [ ] Type styles come from the design system —
      `docs/ralph-workflow-policy/design-system-policy.md`, gate
      `script/design_system_guard.sh`. No ad-hoc font sizes or hex greys.
- [ ] Controls keep their 44px minimum touch target.

### 6. Minutes must meet the course requirement

> **Minutes for activities will equate or surpass total number of minutes
> required for course**

Activity minutes and the plan total already exist. **The only missing piece is
the course-level requirement** — `courses` has no such column.

**Decision: add `courses.required_minutes` (integer, nullable). Warn while
drafting; block at submit-for-approval. Null means no requirement and no gate.**
The requirement belongs to the course, not to one contractor's plan — if each
plan set its own target the constraint would be self-certifying. Blocking every
save would make incremental plan building impossible, so enforcement lands at
the submit gate; null keeps existing courses working unchanged.

Acceptance criteria:

- [ ] `courses.required_minutes` added, nullable, admin-editable.
- [ ] The plan shows running total vs requirement and the shortfall.
- [ ] `totals_min >= required_minutes` is enforced on submit-for-approval;
      short plans are blocked with a message naming the shortfall.
- [ ] Draft saves are never blocked by this rule.
- [ ] `required_minutes IS NULL` → no warning, no gate.
- [ ] Comparison uses `CoursePlan#recompute_totals!` / `totals_min` — do not
      introduce a second summation with different `synthesis` handling.

### 7. Student tab date filter

> **Under student tab have a date filter which allows contractor to select a
> date and student in order to approve work done while student was absent or
> other instances.**

Lives under `app/views/staff/students/`.

Acceptance criteria:

- [ ] Filter selects a date **and** a student.
- [ ] From the filtered view the contractor can approve work for that date.
- [ ] Approval is scoped to the contractor's assigned courses — reuse the
      existing `ContractorCourseAssignment` authorisation, do not widen it.
- [ ] Backdated approval is attributable: it records who approved, when, and
      the date approved *for*.

## Open risks

- **Screenshots not machine-readable here.** Items 3 and 5 were written from the
  surrounding text. Confirm the exact watermark field and type targets against
  Screenshot A/B before editing.
- **Item 1's truncated clause** may have named a fourth symptom beyond the three
  diagnosed. The three above are confirmed in code; if a fourth shows up, report
  it rather than folding it in silently.
- **Item 4 is the largest item** — three input modes, ten slots, upload and
  dictation handling. If it needs splitting, split it and say so.

## Constraints

- Follow `docs/ralph-workflow-policy/` — `design-system-policy.md` for view
  work, `testing-policy.md` before tests, `typechecking-policy.md` for typed
  code (this codebase is `# typed: strict` Sorbet), `security-policy.md` for new
  input surfaces, `verification-policy.md` before reporting completion.
- Never touch production key material: `.kamal/app_secrets/`, `.kamal/secrets`,

  `PROD-SECRET-GUARD` regions in `Dockerfile` and `config/application.rb`.
- `make verify` is the gate. `make help` lists per-gate targets.

## Summary

- [SUM-1] The plan is well characterized overall, but two proven execution gaps leave required mutation and backdated-approval flows unresolved.

## What Came Up Short

- [PA-001] Observation: S-1 defers the known Turbo lock failure to a regression test (“confirm ... whether”); the controllers prove it cannot be fixed by position normalization: every mutation compares the submitted parent lock_version, then advances it, while a Turbo response re-renders only the mutated milestone/activity frame. Cost: the required consecutive mutations on different frames will still return stale-plan 409, so an executor can complete the listed position work without meeting Item 1. Fix: replace the conditional investigation with a concrete response strategy that updates every remaining mutation frame’s lock_version after each successful Turbo mutation (and name the affected milestone/activity response paths and regression tests).
- [PA-002] Observation: S-7 names the approval action and attribution storage as TBD, although the existing route is unusable for the requested contractor flow: ReviewPassesController#create returns forbidden unless the role is men/dex, its sanitize_filters drops date, and Staff::StudentsController#validated_schedule_origin also rejects date. Cost: a date selected on Students cannot survive into the approval pass, and a contractor cannot approve through the only named current path, so the plan provides no executable, authorized route to Item 7’s required dated approval or attribution. Fix: replace S-7’s TBD bullets with the selected controller/route and persistence design, explicitly extend or replace the review-pass authorization with ContractorCourseAssignment-scoped contractor access, carry and validate date through effective_roster_filters, validated_schedule_origin, ReviewPassesController#sanitize_filters, and unit selection, and add positive/negative authorization plus date-attribution tests.

## How To Fix

- [PA-001] Rewrite the S-1 Turbo-frame bullet and its Files/tests list to require the chosen all-live-frame lock-version refresh in both controllers, then prove two distinct existing frames mutate successfully without reload.
- [PA-002] Rewrite S-7 with the concrete dated-approval endpoint/model fields and the full filter/authorization propagation path, then name focused tests that prove a contractor can approve only assigned-course work for the selected date and that the recorded approver, timestamp, and approved-for date are correct.

If the edited draft still has errors it is kept as a draft for further repair and nothing is submitted; the response reports `submitted` either way. Submitting does not end the phase, so a later edit in the same attempt simply resubmits.

Replacing the whole document via `mcp__ralph__ralph_stage_md_artifact` (`mode="replace_all"`) is the fallback when a rewrite really is wholesale — not for a revision whose content is substantially similar to the draft.

Submit a complete plan with `mcp__ralph__ralph_submit_md_artifact`
(`artifact_type="plan"`). For a similar revision, use
`mcp__ralph__ralph_edit_md_artifact` on the staged draft; it resubmits once

# plan artifact format

A plan is one readable Markdown document. Use the structure that makes the
work clearest; headings and step IDs are optional unless a downstream reader
uses them. Keep it short enough to reread, and state each commitment once next
to the work it describes.

## The only blocking rule

`PLAN001` is the sole error. It means the submission is not a plan: it is
empty or markup-only, has fewer than 100 characters of actual content, is
recognizably truncated (an unterminated frontmatter block, unclosed code fence,
dangling plan field label, final comma or function word, unclosed inline
bracket/parenthesis/backtick, or empty list bullet at EOF), or is clearly a
refusal, question, status update,
tool output, stack trace, or placeholder. Analysis and execution cannot proceed
without a plan to read.

Every other finding is advisory:

- **Warning** predicts a concrete cost to this run and says how to resolve it.
- **Info** is an observation worth a second look.

Warnings and info never make a plan invalid. If proceeding is the informed
choice, record the reason under `## Validation Overrides` as
`- [RULE-ID] reason`. Override reasons remain visible in tool responses and
plan history; stale overrides are reported as info.

## Useful default shape

A good plan normally makes four phases visible in the order they will happen:
Orient, Characterize current behavior, Change, and Verify. It should state the
outcome, real files or areas already inspected, risks or unknowns, and
completion evidence. These are authoring guidance, not required headings.

```markdown
---
type: plan
---
## Work

### [S-1] Characterize the current retry behavior
Inspect the current default and add a focused regression that captures it.

Files:
- modify tests/test_retry.py

### [S-2] Change and prove the default
Update the retry implementation and run the focused test.

Files:
- modify ralph/retry.py
Depends on: S-1
Verify: pytest tests/test_retry.py -q
Expect: the focused retry tests pass with exit code 0
```

Custom headings, prose plans, and an omitted conventional section are valid
when the plan remains understandable. For a larger conventional sample, see
`.agent/artifact-formats/examples/plan.md`. For parallel work, use `## Work Units`
or `## Parallel Plan` only when the executor will consume those markers;
otherwise describe independent work naturally.

## Standard artifact tools

Submit a complete document with `ralph_submit_md_artifact` using
`artifact_type: plan`; `ralph_verify_md_artifact` previews the same result.
For a similar revision, use `ralph_edit_md_artifact` on the staged draft. It
submits automatically when the edited draft has no errors. Use
`ralph_stage_md_artifact` with `mode="replace_all"` only for a wholesale rewrite;
inspect with `ralph_get_md_draft` and submit an assembled draft with
`ralph_finalize_md_artifact`. Staging is not submission: a retained draft that
differs from the canonical document blocks phase completion until it is
resubmitted or deliberately abandoned with `ralph_discard_md_draft`.

Do not write `.agent/artifacts/plan.md` directly. After a valid submission,
call `declare_complete` as the final action.

# typed: strict

class CoursePlanMilestonesController < ApplicationController
  extend T::Sig

  before_action :load_course_plan
  before_action :load_milestone, only: %i[update destroy reorder]
  around_action :lock_course_plan_for_mutation
  rescue_from ActiveRecord::StaleObjectError, with: :render_stale_plan

  sig { void }
  def create
    course_plan = T.must(@course_plan)
    milestone = course_plan.course_plan_milestones.build(milestone_params.merge(position: next_position))

    if milestone.save
      respond_to_milestone_mutation(course_plan, milestone, "Milestone added.")
    elsif turbo_frame_request?
      render_milestone_errors(course_plan, milestone)
    else
      flash[:course_plan_milestone_title_attempt] = milestone.title.to_s
      redirect_to support_course_plan_path(course_plan), alert: milestone.errors.full_messages.to_sentence
    end
  end

  sig { void }
  def update
    course_plan = T.must(@course_plan)
    milestone = T.must(@milestone)
    milestone.assign_attributes(milestone_params)

    if milestone.save
      respond_to_milestone_mutation(course_plan, milestone, "Milestone updated.")
    elsif turbo_frame_request?
      render_milestone_errors(course_plan, milestone)
    else
      redirect_to support_course_plan_path(course_plan, anchor: "course-plan-milestone-#{milestone.id}"), alert: milestone.errors.full_messages.to_sentence
    end
  end

  sig { void }
  def destroy
    course_plan = T.must(@course_plan)
    milestone = T.must(@milestone)
    discarded_at = Time.current
    milestone.update!(discarded_at:)
    CoursePlanActivity.where(course_plan_milestone_id: milestone.id, discarded_at: nil).update_all(discarded_at:, cascade_discarded_at: discarded_at)
    course_plan.recompute_totals!
    redirect_to support_course_plan_path(course_plan), notice: "Milestone removed.", alert: nil
  end

  sig { void }
  def restore
    course_plan = T.must(@course_plan)
    milestone = CoursePlanMilestone.unscoped.where(course_plan: course_plan).find_by(id: params[:id], discarded_at: ..Time.current)
    raise ActiveRecord::RecordNotFound unless milestone

    cascade_marker = milestone.discarded_at
    milestone.update!(discarded_at: nil)
    CoursePlanActivity.where(course_plan_milestone_id: milestone.id, cascade_discarded_at: cascade_marker).update_all(discarded_at: nil, cascade_discarded_at: nil)
    course_plan.course_plan_milestones.reorder(:position, :id).each_with_index do |sibling, index|
      sibling.update_columns(position: index)
    end
    course_plan.recompute_totals!
    redirect_to support_course_plan_path(course_plan, anchor: "course-plan-milestone-#{milestone.id}"), notice: "Milestone restored."
  end


  sig { void }
  def reorder
    course_plan = T.must(@course_plan)
    milestone = T.must(@milestone)
    reorder_milestones!(milestone, requested_position)
    redirect_to support_course_plan_path(course_plan, anchor: "course-plan-milestone-#{milestone.id}"), notice: "Milestone reordered."
  end

  private

  sig { void }
  def load_course_plan
    @course_plan = T.let(authorize_course_plan(params[:course_plan_id]), T.nilable(CoursePlan))
    course_plan = @course_plan
    raise ActiveRecord::RecordNotFound unless course_plan && (course_plan.draft? || course_plan.needs_revision?)
  end

  sig { void }
  def verify_course_plan_lock
    raw_lock_version = params[:lock_version].to_s
    course_plan = T.must(@course_plan)
    # DA-006 — a missing or empty lock_version is rejected for
    # EVERY mutation, including create/destroy/reorder/duplicate/
    # reassign/restore. The prior "skip when empty and not
    # update" exception let stale create/destroy requests race in
    # against the latest plan and overwrite newer edits; we now
    # require the parent lock version on every child write.
    if raw_lock_version.empty?
      raise ActiveRecord::StaleObjectError.new(course_plan, action_name.to_s)
    end
    raise ActiveRecord::StaleObjectError.new(course_plan, action_name.to_s) unless raw_lock_version.match?(/\A\d+\z/) && raw_lock_version.to_i == course_plan.lock_version
  end

  sig { params(action: T.proc.void).void }
  def lock_course_plan_for_mutation(&action)
    course_plan = T.must(@course_plan)
    course_plan.with_lock do
      verify_course_plan_lock
      initial_lock_version = course_plan.lock_version
      action.call
      course_plan.reload
      course_plan.touch if (response.successful? || response.redirect?) && course_plan.lock_version == initial_lock_version
    end
  end

  sig { void }
  def load_milestone
    @milestone = T.let(T.must(@course_plan).course_plan_milestones.find_by(id: params[:id]), T.nilable(CoursePlanMilestone))
    raise ActiveRecord::RecordNotFound unless @milestone
  end

  sig { params(id: Object).returns(T.nilable(CoursePlan)) }
  def authorize_course_plan(id)
    actor = current_user || raise(ActiveRecord::RecordNotFound)
    site = current_active_site || raise(ActiveRecord::RecordNotFound)
    return nil unless current_active_role == :con

    CoursePlan.where(site: site, author: actor,
                     course_id: ContractorCourseAssignment.where(contractor_user: actor, site: site).select(:course_id)).find_by(id: id)
  end

  sig { returns(Integer) }
  def next_position
    T.must(@course_plan).course_plan_milestones.maximum(:position).to_i + 1
  end

  sig { returns(Integer) }
  def requested_position
    raw_position = params[:position].to_s
    raw_position.match?(/\A\d+\z/) ? raw_position.to_i : T.must(@milestone).position
  end

  sig { params(milestone: CoursePlanMilestone, position: Integer).void }
  def reorder_milestones!(milestone, position)
    milestone.class.transaction do
      siblings = T.must(@course_plan).course_plan_milestones.reorder(:position, :id).to_a
      target = position.clamp(0, siblings.length - 1)
      siblings.delete(milestone)
      siblings.insert(target, milestone)
      siblings.each_with_index { |sibling, index| sibling.update_columns(position: index) }
    end
  end

  sig { params(_error: ActiveRecord::StaleObjectError).void }
  def render_stale_plan(_error)
    return if performed?

    if turbo_frame_request?
      render partial: "shared/plan_builder/stale_mutation", locals: { course_plan: T.must(@course_plan), frame_id: request.headers.fetch("Turbo-Frame") }, status: :conflict
    else
      redirect_to support_course_plan_path(T.must(@course_plan)), alert: "This plan changed in another session. Reload it and try again.", status: :conflict
    end
  end

  sig { returns(T::Boolean) }
  def turbo_frame_request?
    request.headers["Turbo-Frame"].present?
  end

  sig { params(course_plan: CoursePlan, milestone: CoursePlanMilestone, notice: String).void }
  def respond_to_milestone_mutation(course_plan, milestone, notice)
    if turbo_frame_request?
      # Keep the returned milestone frame usable for its next mutation by
      # rendering its hidden lock version after advancing the parent plan.
      prepare_turbo_success!(course_plan)
      render partial: "shared/plan_builder/course_milestone", locals: { course_plan:, milestone:, presenter: PlanBuilderPresenter.new(plan: course_plan, variant: :course, current_user: current_user), notice: }
    else
      redirect_to support_course_plan_path(course_plan, anchor: "course-plan-milestone-#{milestone.id}"), notice:
    end
  end

  sig { params(course_plan: CoursePlan).void }
  def prepare_turbo_success!(course_plan)
    course_plan.reload
    course_plan.touch
    course_plan.reload
  end

  sig { params(course_plan: CoursePlan, milestone: CoursePlanMilestone).void }
  def render_milestone_errors(course_plan, milestone)
    render partial: "shared/plan_builder/course_milestone", locals: { course_plan:, milestone:, presenter: PlanBuilderPresenter.new(plan: course_plan, variant: :course, current_user: current_user) }, status: :unprocessable_entity
  end

  sig { returns(ActionController::Parameters) }
  def milestone_params
    params.require(:course_plan_milestone).permit(:title, :product)
  end
end

class CoursePlanActivitiesController < ApplicationController
  extend T::Sig

  before_action :load_course_plan
  before_action :load_milestone
  before_action :load_activity, only: %i[update destroy reorder duplicate reassign]
  around_action :lock_course_plan_for_mutation
  rescue_from ActiveRecord::StaleObjectError, with: :render_stale_plan

  sig { void }
  def create
    course_plan = T.must(@course_plan)
    activity = T.must(@milestone).course_plan_activities.build(activity_params.merge(course_plan: course_plan, position: next_position))

    if activity.save
      course_plan.recompute_totals!
      respond_to_activity_create(course_plan, activity)
    elsif turbo_frame_request?
      render partial: "shared/plan_builder/course_milestone", locals: { course_plan:, milestone: T.must(@milestone), presenter: PlanBuilderPresenter.new(plan: course_plan, variant: :course, current_user: current_user), new_activity: activity }, status: :unprocessable_entity
    else
      redirect_to support_course_plan_path(course_plan, anchor: "course-plan-milestone-#{T.must(@milestone).id}"), alert: activity.errors.full_messages.to_sentence
    end
  end

  sig { void }
  def update
    course_plan = T.must(@course_plan)
    activity = T.must(@activity)
    activity.assign_attributes(activity_params)

    if activity.save
      course_plan.recompute_totals!
      respond_to_activity_update(course_plan, activity)
    elsif turbo_frame_request?
      render_activity_update_errors(course_plan, activity)
    else
      redirect_to support_course_plan_path(course_plan, anchor: "course-plan-activity-#{activity.id}"), alert: activity.errors.full_messages.to_sentence
    end
  end

  sig { void }
  def duplicate
    course_plan = T.must(@course_plan)
    source = T.must(@activity)
    duplicate = T.must(@milestone).course_plan_activities.create!(
      course_plan: course_plan,
      title: "#{source.title} (copy)",
      description: source.description,
      time_value_min: source.time_value_min,
      position: next_position
    )
    course_plan.recompute_totals!
    redirect_to support_course_plan_path(course_plan, anchor: "course-plan-activity-#{duplicate.id}"), notice: "Activity duplicated."
  end

  sig { void }
  def reassign
    course_plan = T.must(@course_plan)
    activity = T.must(@activity)
    destination = course_plan.course_plan_milestones.find_by(id: reassignment_milestone_id)
    raise ActiveRecord::RecordNotFound unless destination

    CoursePlanActivity.transaction do
      activity.update!(course_plan_milestone: destination, position: destination.course_plan_activities.maximum(:position).to_i + 1)
      normalize_positions!(T.must(@milestone))
      normalize_positions!(destination)
      course_plan.recompute_totals!
    end
    redirect_to support_course_plan_path(course_plan, anchor: "course-plan-activity-#{activity.id}"), notice: "Activity reassigned."
  end

  sig { void }
  def destroy
    course_plan = T.must(@course_plan)
    activity = T.must(@activity)
    activity.update!(discarded_at: Time.current, cascade_discarded_at: nil)
    course_plan.recompute_totals!
    redirect_to support_course_plan_path(course_plan), notice: "Activity removed."
  end

  sig { void }
  def restore
    course_plan = T.must(@course_plan)
    milestone = course_plan.course_plan_milestones.find_by(id: params[:milestone_id])
    raise ActiveRecord::RecordNotFound unless milestone

    activity = CoursePlanActivity.unscoped.where(course_plan: course_plan, course_plan_milestone: milestone).find_by(id: params[:id], discarded_at: ..Time.current)
    raise ActiveRecord::RecordNotFound unless activity

    activity.update!(discarded_at: nil, cascade_discarded_at: nil)
    milestone.course_plan_activities.reorder(:position, :id).each_with_index do |sibling, index|
      sibling.update_columns(position: index)
    end
    course_plan.recompute_totals!
    redirect_to support_course_plan_path(course_plan, anchor: "course-plan-activity-#{activity.id}"), notice: "Activity restored."
  end

  sig { void }

    reorder_activities!(activity, requested_position)

  end

  sig { void }
  def load_activity
    @activity = T.let(T.must(@milestone).course_plan_activities.find_by(id: params[:id]), T.nilable(CoursePlanActivity))
    raise ActiveRecord::RecordNotFound unless @activity
  end

  sig { returns(Integer) }
  def next_position
    T.must(@milestone).course_plan_activities.maximum(:position).to_i + 1
  end

    raw_id = params.require(:course_plan_activity).permit(:course_plan_milestone_id)[:course_plan_milestone_id].to_s
    raise ActiveRecord::RecordNotFound unless raw_id.match?(/\A\d+\z/)

    raw_id.to_i

    course_plan = T.must(@course_plan)

    if activity.save
      course_plan.recompute_totals!
      respond_to_activity_create(course_plan, activity)
    elsif turbo_frame_request?
      render partial: "shared/plan_builder/course_milestone", locals: { course_plan:, milestone: T.must(@milestone), presenter: PlanBuilderPresenter.new(plan: course_plan, variant: :course, current_user: current_user), new_activity: activity }, status: :unprocessable_entity
    else
      redirect_to support_course_plan_path(course_plan, anchor: "course-plan-milestone-#{T.must(@milestone).id}"), alert: activity.errors.full_messages.to_sentence
    end
  end

  sig { void }
  def update
    course_plan = T.must(@course_plan)
    activity = T.must(@activity)
    activity.assign_attributes(activity_params)

    if activity.save
      course_plan.recompute_totals!
      respond_to_activity_update(course_plan, activity)
    elsif turbo_frame_request?
      render_activity_update_errors(course_plan, activity)
    else

    end
  end

    course_plan = T.must(@course_plan)
    source = T.must(@activity)
    duplicate = T.must(@milestone).course_plan_activities.create!(

content.text:
# typed: strict

# WT-09 / S-6 — Review pass controller for sequential decision
# flow on the mentor surfaces (Students → pick a student and a
# review type → decide → next).
#
# A pass is opened (POST /review_passes) by the roster heading
# (column-name with the count, opens every waiting student in
# the current filter+sort) or by the signoff list
# `Review readiness ({n})` heading control (readiness pass
# over the current filter+sort). Decision URLs carry the pass
# id; the existing decision endpoints use the pass id to know
# which unit comes next.
#
# Authorization scope: MEN / DEX only. SUP is rejected (RC-65
# operational-inspection branch is read-only). CON / STU are
# bounced to /denied. The pass id is treated as opaque to
# callers (no enumeration); the controller loads it by id and
# verifies ownership against `current_user.id` so a mentor
# cannot poke another mentor's pass.
class ReviewPassesController < ApplicationController
  extend T::Sig

  ALLOWED_ORIGINS = T.let(%w[students_heading students_cell signoff_heading direct cell_pass].freeze, T::Array[String])
  ALLOWED_REVIEW_TYPES = T.let(%w[plan evidence final_product readiness].freeze, T::Array[String])
  ALLOWED_RETURN_PATHS = T.let(%w[/students /signoff /review/plans /review/evidence /review/final-products].freeze, T::Array[String])

  before_action :require_credit_authority

  # POST /review_passes
  # Opens a new pass. Any existing active pass for the
  # (actor, role, review_type, site) tuple is abandoned with
  # reason `superseded` so the new pass replaces it cleanly.
  #
  # DA-003 (analysis feedback) — derive and validate the
  # replacement membership BEFORE superseding the existing
  # active pass. The prior flow abandoned the active pass first
  # and then built units, so a request whose filtered projection
  # was empty destroyed resumable active work and opened an
  # unusable ended pass. Now an empty replacement is detected
  # up front and the existing active pass is left untouched
  # (still resumable), matching §6's "offered back" contract.
  sig { void }
  def create
    return head(:forbidden) unless %i[men dex].include?(current_active_role)

    review_type = params[:review_type].to_s
    return head(:bad_request) unless ALLOWED_REVIEW_TYPES.include?(review_type)
    origin = params[:origin].to_s
    return head(:bad_request) unless ALLOWED_ORIGINS.include?(origin)
    origin_path = sanitize_origin_path(params[:origin_path])

    acting_role = current_active_role
    site = current_active_site

    filters = sanitize_filters(params[:filters])
    units = build_units_for(review_type.to_sym, site: site, origin: origin, filters: filters)
    units = suffix_units_from_anchor(units, origin: origin, anchor_student_id: params[:anchor_student_id])

    existing = ReviewPass.active_for(actor: T.must(current_user), acting_role: T.must(acting_role), review_type: review_type.to_sym, site: site)

    # DA-003 (analysis feedback) — an empty replacement must not destroy
    # resumable active work. If the mentor already has an active pass for
    # this (role, review_type, site) and the new filtered projection is
    # empty, leave the existing pass untouched (still resumable) and
    # return the mentor to the origin so they can resume or adjust
    # filters. The prior flow abandoned the active pass first and then
    # discovered the empty membership, destroying resumable work without
    # opening a usable replacement. When there is no existing active pass,
    # an empty projection still records an ended empty pass so the mentor
    # sees the "nothing waiting" outcome rather than a silent no-op.
    if units.empty? && existing
      flash[:notice] = "No waiting work matches these filters. Your existing pass is still available."
      redirect_to origin_path || review_path
      return
    end

    ReviewPass.transaction do
      existing&.abandon!(reason: "superseded")

      pass = ReviewPass.create!(
        actor_id: T.must(current_user).id,
        site_id: site&.id || 0,
        acting_role: acting_role.to_s,
        review_type: review_type,
        origin: origin,
        origin_path: origin_path,
        filters: filters,
        total_units: 0,
        current_position: 0,
        ended: false
      )

      units.each_with_index do |attrs, idx|
        pass.review_pass_units.create!(
          unit_kind: attrs.fetch(:unit_kind),
          position: idx + 1,
          student_id: attrs[:student_id],
          submission_id: attrs[:submission_id],
          plan_id: attrs[:plan_id],
          plan_activity_id: attrs[:plan_activity_id]
        )
      end

      pass.update!(total_units: units.size)

      if units.empty?
        pass.update!(ended: true, ended_at: Time.current, ending_reason: "externally_completed")
        redirect_to origin_path || review_path
      else
        first = T.must(units.first)
        pass.update!(
          current_unit_kind: first.fetch(:unit_kind),
          current_unit_id: case first[:unit_kind]
                           when "student" then first[:student_id]
                           when "submission" then first[:submission_id]
                           when "plan" then first[:plan_id]
                           when "plan_activity" then first[:plan_activity_id]
                           else nil
                           end,
          current_position: 1
        )
        redirect_to decision_url_for(pass, first)
      end
    end
  end

  # GET /review_passes/:id
  # Resume a pass. Re-opens the current unit so a mentor can
  # bookmark or reload without losing the pass.
  sig { void }
  def show
    pass = scoped_pass
    return head(:not_found) unless pass
    return head(:forbidden) unless pass.acting_role == current_active_role.to_s
    return head(:forbidden) unless pass.site_id == current_active_site&.id
    return head(:gone) unless pass.active?

    unit = pass.current_unit_row
    if unit.nil?
      redirect_to (pass.origin_path.presence || review_path)
      return
    end

    redirect_to decision_url_for(pass, unit)
  end

  # POST /review_passes/:id/resume
  # Explicitly reactivates an abandoned pass for its owner. This preserves the
  # membership and current position captured when the pass began; completed
  # passes remain terminal.
  sig { void }
  def resume
    pass = scoped_pass
    return head(:not_found) unless pass
    return head(:forbidden) unless pass.acting_role == current_active_role.to_s
    return head(:forbidden) unless pass.site_id == current_active_site&.id
    return head(:gone) unless pass.resume!

    unit = pass.current_unit_row
    if unit
      redirect_to decision_url_for(pass, unit)
    else
      redirect_to (pass.origin_path.presence || review_path)
    end
  end

  # POST /review_passes/:id/skip
  # Skip current unit (does not record an outcome; moves the
  # unit to the end of the pass's visit order).
  sig { void }
  def skip
    pass = scoped_pass
    return head(:not_found) unless pass
    return head(:forbidden) unless pass.acting_role == current_active_role.to_s
    return head(:forbidden) unless pass.site_id == current_active_site&.id
    return head(:gone) unless pass.active?

    pass.skip_current!

    next_unit = pass.current_unit_row
    if next_unit
      redirect_to decision_url_for(pass, next_unit)
    else
      redirect_to (pass.origin_path.presence || review_path)
    end
  end

  # POST /review_passes/:id/end_pass
  # Confirm end of a pass with units remaining. DA-003 (analysis
  # feedback) — this public endpoint is constrained to the ONE
  # client-initiated ending path from §6 ("the mentor confirms
  # leaving") and to an ACTIVE pass only. The other four ending
  # reasons are server-owned: `completed` and `all_skipped` are
  # derived in ReviewPass#advance! / #skip_current!,
  # `returned_to_students` is derived in the review-screen
  # outcome transitions, and `externally_completed` is derived
  # when remaining units are completed by other reviewers. The
  # prior implementation accepted every client-supplied
  # ENDING_REASONS value and rewrote inactive passes via #end!,
  # letting a caller claim a server-derived reason or rewrite a
  # terminal pass. Now only `confirmed_end` against an active
  # pass is honored; any other reason or an inactive pass is
  # rejected with 400 / 410 so the audit trail stays honest.
  sig { void }
  def end_pass
    pass = scoped_pass
    return head(:not_found) unless pass
    return head(:forbidden) unless pass.acting_role == current_active_role.to_s
    return head(:forbidden) unless pass.site_id == current_active_site&.id
    return head(:gone) unless pass.active?

    reason = params[:reason].to_s.presence || "confirmed_end"
    return head(:bad_request) unless reason == "confirmed_end"

    pass.abandon!(reason: reason)
    redirect_to (pass.origin_path.presence || review_path)
  end

  # DELETE /review_passes/:id
  # Hard-reset (admin / out-of-band). Not normally used by the
  # mentor surfaces — the controllers themselves call
  # ReviewPass#advance! / #end! / #abandon! in-line so the
  # audit trail stays inside the decision rows.

  # unknown id OR a pass that does not belong to the current
  # user — both surface as 404 so an attacker cannot enumerate

  # paths, and any path outside the allowlist. The allowlist
  # covers the seven screens in §5 plus the three review
  # screens which remain reachable as direct links.

  def sanitize_origin_path(path)

  # canonical waiting-set computation lives in the server-side scope and
  # filtered projection. Request parameters may describe filters and origin,
  # but never membership: a pass always freezes every currently eligible unit
  # in that authorized projection.
  sig do

      origin: String,

    when :plan
      build_plan_units(site: site, filters: filters)
    when :evidence
      build_evidence_units(site: site, filters: filters)
    when :final_product
      build_final_product_units(site: site, filters: filters)

  end

    params(
      site: T.nilable(Site),

    ).returns(T::Array[T::Hash[Symbol, T.nilable(Integer)]])
  end
  def build_plan_units(site:, filters:)
    scope = Reviews::QueueScope.new(user: current_user, site: site, role: current_active_role, today: site&.today || Date.current)
    plans = apply_pass_filters(
      scope.plans(status: :submitted_for_approval).where.not(mentor_example: true),
      filters: filters,
      review_type: :plan

    # work for MEN, but it must not be included in a fresh DEX pass.

    if filters[:class_id].to_s.match?(/\A[1-9]\d*\z/)
      relation = if review_type == :plan
        relation.where(school_class_id: filters[:class_id].to_s.to_i)
      else
        relation.where(plans: { school_class_id: filters[:class_id].to_s.to_i })
      end
    end

      relation = if review_type == :plan

      else

    else
      base
    end
  end

# flow on the mentor surfaces (Students → pick a student and a
# review type → decide → next).

# A pass is opened (POST /review_passes) by the roster heading
# (column-name with the count, opens every waiting student in
# the current filter+sort) or by the signoff list

# over the current filter+sort). Decision URLs carry the pass
# id; the existing decision endpoints use the pass id to know
# which unit comes next.
#

# operational-inspection branch is read-only). CON / STU are
# bounced to /denied. The pass id is treated as opaque to
# callers (no enumeration); the controller loads it by id and
# verifies ownership against `current_user.id` so a mentor
# cannot poke another mentor's pass.

  ALLOWED_ORIGINS = T.let(%w[students_heading students_cell signoff_heading direct cell_pass].freeze, T::Array[String])
  ALLOWED_REVIEW_TYPES = T.let(%w[plan evidence final_product readiness].freeze, T::Array[String])

  # POST /review_passes

  # (actor, role, review_type, site) tuple is abandoned with
  # reason `superseded` so the new pass replaces it cleanly.
  #
  # DA-003 (analysis feedback) — derive and validate the
  # replacement membership BEFORE superseding the existing
  # active pass. The prior flow abandoned the active pass first
  # and then built units, so a request whose filtered projection
  # was empty destroyed resumable active work and opened an
  # unusable ended pass. Now an empty replacement is detected
  # up front and the existing active pass is left untouched
  # (still resumable), matching §6's "offered back" contract.
  sig { void }
  def create
    return head(:forbidden) unless %i[men dex].include?(current_active_role)

    review_type = params[:review_type].to_s
    return head(:bad_request) unless ALLOWED_REVIEW_TYPES.include?(review_type)

    existing = ReviewPass.active_for(actor: T.must(current_user), acting_role: T.must(acting_role), review_type: review_type.to_sym, site: site)

    # resumable active work. If the mentor already has an active pass for
    # this (role, review_type, site) and the new filtered projection is
    # empty, leave the existing pass untouched (still resumable) and
    # return the mentor to the origin so they can resume or adjust
    # filters. The prior flow abandoned the active pass first and then
    # discovered the empty membership, destroying resumable work without
    # opening a usable replacement. When there is no existing active pass,
    # an empty projection still records an ended empty pass so the mentor
    # sees the "nothing waiting" outcome rather than a silent no-op.

      redirect_to origin_path || review_path

      existing&.abandon!(reason: "superseded")

        review_type: review_type,
        origin: origin,
        origin_path: origin_path,

        total_units: 0,
        current_position: 0,

          unit_kind: attrs.fetch(:unit_kind),

          student_id: attrs[:student_id],

      else

          current_unit_kind: first.fetch(:unit_kind),

                           when "submission" then first[:submission_id]
                           when "plan" then first[:plan_id]
                           when "plan_activity" then first[:plan_activity_id]

  end
  def build_evidence_units(site:, filters:)
    scope = Reviews::QueueScope.new(user: current_user, site: site, role: current_active_role, today: site&.today || Date.current)
    rows = apply_pass_filters(scope.evidence, filters: filters, review_type: :evidence).pluck(:id, :student_id)
    rows.map { |submission_id, student_id| { unit_kind: "submission", submission_id: submission_id, student_id: student_id } }
  end

  sig do
    params(
      site: T.nilable(Site),
      filters: T::Hash[Symbol, Object]
    ).returns(T::Array[T::Hash[Symbol, T.nilable(Integer)]])
  end
  def build_final_product_units(site:, filters:)
    scope = Reviews::QueueScope.new(user: current_user, site: site, role: current_active_role, today: site&.today || Date.current)
    role_tier = current_active_role == :men ? :grant : :recommendation
    reviewed_submission_ids = FinalProductReview.with_outcome.where(tier: role_tier).select(:submission_id)
    rows = apply_pass_filters(scope.final_products.where.not(id: reviewed_submission_ids), filters: filters, review_type: :final_product).pluck(:id, :student_id)
    rows.map { |submission_id, student_id| { unit_kind: "submission", submission_id: submission_id, student_id: student_id } }
  end

  sig do
    params(
      site: T.nilable(Site),
      filters: T::Hash[Symbol, Object]
    ).returns(T::Array[T::Hash[Symbol, T.nilable(Integer)]])
  end
  def build_readiness_units(site:, filters:)
    scope = Reviews::QueueScope.new(user: current_user, site: site, role: current_active_role, today: site&.today || Date.current)
    round = scope.current_signoff_round
    ids = round ? apply_pass_filters(scope.signoff_candidates(round: round), filters: filters, review_type: :readiness).pluck(:id) : []
    ids.map { |student_id| { unit_kind: "student", student_id: student_id } }
  end

  # The pass must capture only actionable units in the authorized filtered
  # projection. Statuses other than Waiting cannot create a pass.
  sig do
    params(
      relation: ActiveRecord::Relation,
      filters: T::Hash[Symbol, Object],
      review_type: Symbol
    ).returns(ActiveRecord::Relation)
  end
  def apply_pass_filters(relation, filters:, review_type:)
    selected_type = filters[:review_type].to_s
    selected_status = filters[:status].to_s
    return relation.none if selected_type.present? && selected_type != review_type.to_s
    # A pass contains waiting units only. Other roster status filters are
    # useful for inspection but cannot legitimately start a waiting pass.
    return relation.none if selected_status.present? && selected_status != "waiting"

    if review_type == :readiness
      relation = relation.where(id: filters[:student_id].to_s.to_i) if filters[:student_id].to_s.match?(/\A[1-9]\d*\z/)
      class_filter_id = filters[:school_class_id].presence || filters[:class_id]
      if class_filter_id.to_s.match?(/\A[1-9]\d*\z/)
        enrolled_ids = Enrollment.active_on(current_active_site&.today || Date.current, site: current_active_site)
                                .where(school_class_id: class_filter_id.to_s.to_i)
                                .select(:student_id)
        relation = relation.where(id: enrolled_ids)
      end
      return relation.where(id: Plan.where(round_id: filters[:round_id].to_s.to_i).select(:student_id)) if filters[:round_id].to_s.match?(/\A[1-9]\d*\z/)

      return relation
    end

    relation = relation.where(student_id: filters[:student_id].to_s.to_i) if filters[:student_id].to_s.match?(/\A[1-9]\d*\z/)
    if filters[:class_id].to_s.match?(/\A[1-9]\d*\z/)
      relation = if review_type == :plan
        relation.where(school_class_id: filters[:class_id].to_s.to_i)
      else
        relation.where(plans: { school_class_id: filters[:class_id].to_s.to_i })
      end
    end
    if filters[:round_id].to_s.match?(/\A[1-9]\d*\z/)
      relation = if review_type == :plan
        relation.where(round_id: filters[:round_id].to_s.to_i)
      else
        relation.where(rounds: { id: filters[:round_id].to_s.to_i })
      end
    end
    relation
  end


  # A waiting roster cell starts at its own student and retains only the
  # projection suffix after it. The request may name the anchor student but
  # never pass ids or membership; membership/order remain server-derived.
  sig do
    params(
      units: T::Array[T::Hash[Symbol, T.nilable(Integer)]],
      origin: String,
      anchor_student_id: T.nilable(Object)
    ).returns(T::Array[T::Hash[Symbol, T.nilable(Integer)]])
  end
  def suffix_units_from_anchor(units, origin:, anchor_student_id:)
    return units unless %w[students_cell cell_pass].include?(origin)
    return [] unless anchor_student_id.to_s.match?(/\A[1-9]\d*\z/)

    anchor_id = anchor_student_id.to_s.to_i
    anchor_index = units.index { |unit| unit_student_id(unit) == anchor_id }
    anchor_index ? units.drop(anchor_index) : []
  end

  sig { params(unit: T::Hash[Symbol, T.nilable(Integer)]).returns(T.nilable(Integer)) }
  def unit_student_id(unit)
    unit[:student_id]
  end

  sig do
    params(
      pass: ReviewPass,
      unit: T.any(T::Hash[Symbol, T.nilable(Integer)], ReviewPassUnit)
    ).returns(String)
  end
  def decision_url_for(pass, unit)
    unit_kind = unit.is_a?(Hash) ? unit[:unit_kind] : unit.unit_kind
    plan_id = unit.is_a?(Hash) ? unit[:plan_id] : unit.plan_id
    submission_id = unit.is_a?(Hash) ? unit[:submission_id] : unit.submission_id
    student_id = unit.is_a?(Hash) ? unit[:student_id] : unit.student_id

    base = case pass.review_type
    when "plan" then "/review/plans"
    when "evidence" then "/review"
    when "final_product" then "/review/final-products"
    when "readiness" then "/review/students/#{student_id}/portfolio"
    else "/students"
    end

    case unit_kind
    when "plan"
      "/review/plans/#{plan_id}?pass_id=#{pass.id}"
    when "submission"
      if pass.review_type == "final_product"
        "/review/final-products/#{submission_id}?pass_id=#{pass.id}"
      else
        "/review/#{submission_id}?pass_id=#{pass.id}"
      end
    when "student"
      "/review/students/#{student_id}/portfolio?pass_id=#{pass.id}"
    else
      base
    end
  end
end
